🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Matthew Wright, a longtime executive producer of The Ellen DeGeneres Show who often appeared on camera alongside its host, has died at 52.

Wright died on October 30, 2026, while working remotely in Los Angeles, according to a family fundraising page set up after his death. The page described his death as an "unfathomable tragedy." No cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Ellen DeGeneres paid tribute to Wright in a video posted on November 2, 2026, calling him "the glue" of the show's family and saying "everyone loved him." She said his sudden death was "shocking" and that the two had been getting ready to start another project together.

Wright joined The Ellen DeGeneres Show in 2006 and stayed with the daytime talk show for 16 years, until it ended in 2022, serving in several production roles including executive producer. He frequently appeared in on-air bits with DeGeneres. After the show ended, he worked as a consulting producer for The Jennifer Hudson Show and as a senior supervising producer for The Drew Barrymore Show.

He is survived by his husband, Justin Fusella. His family is raising funds to bring him home to New York for a funeral and to hold a memorial in Los Angeles.

Rest in Peace, Matthew Wright.

Sources: USA Today; TheWrap; Parade.
